what: Symbotic builds warehouse automation. Its robots move cases and pallets around distribution centres, building mixed pallets automatically for store delivery. Walmart is by far its largest customer.
customers: Large retailers and wholesalers automating their distribution centres, led by Walmart, plus a joint venture with SoftBank.
money: designing, building and installing automated warehouse systems
recurring support and operation of installed systems
moat: A fully integrated robotics and software system proven at the scale of the world's largest retailer, which takes years to design, install and commission.
risks: Walmart accounts for the large majority of revenue, an extreme concentration
Gross margin of 19% is thin for a technology company and installations have had cost overruns
It has barely broken even and has restated results in the past
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 26% last year and about 56% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Recurring software and operation revenue grows as more systems come online
watch: Customer concentration, backlog, and gross margin on installations.
